requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
rationale:
**Implementation.** The only `{impl}` site is `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md`. It is declared with `:impl:` on the requirement in `md/requirements/cli.md`. The skill is bundled because `Cargo.toml` publishes everything under `assets/skills` through `[[package.metadata.symposium.skills]]`. The requirement's obligations map to the skill text as follows:
- **Read code and tests.** The skill's first paragraph says to read existing requirements, documentation, public entry points, implementation and tests, and to "follow behavior through the code".
- **Map every first-party test.** The first inventory covers "every first-party runnable test or test case", including doctests and parameterized cases. It requires at least one `{test}` reference with a full requirement or example name on each test, and it forbids a file-level tag standing in for unrelated tests.
- **Map every end-user-visible source unit.** The second inventory covers every explicit Rust function or method. It also covers public APIs, commands, handlers, UI actions, configuration, outputs, errors and observable branches. It requires `{impl}`, `{test}` or `{cite}` references on each function, says a tagged entry point does not cover deeper code, and says there is no waiver.
- **Report gaps and require independent review.** The skill says to "Have both inventories independently reviewed against the source and tests before claiming complete coverage". It allows claiming 100% only when neither inventory has unmapped items, and it requires listing remaining gaps with locations and reasons without silently excluding hard cases.

The skill also covers other behaviour: user agreement on proposed requirements, running `habeas author --all`, and what the harness assesses. Other requirements specify that behaviour: `requirements_review_skill`, `internal_detail_guidance`, `behavior_review_guidance` and `authoring.batch`. Those requirements also carry `:impl:` anchors on this file. The guidance to exclude generated and third-party code is a small extension. It is consistent with the requirement's "first-party" scope and is not an unspecified end-user-observable behaviour.

**Tests.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs::bootstrap_skill_is_bundled_and_directs_complete_inventories` is tagged `{test}` for this requirement. It checks these points:
- `Cargo.toml` publishes `assets/skills` for Symposium, so the skill is bundled.
- The skill file has the expected front matter name and description.
- The skill contains phrases for each obligation: read code and tests, the test inventory and `{test}` tagging, the function inventory and attached references, independent review before claiming completeness, and reporting gaps.

The helpers `bundled_skill` and `assert_phrases` are also tagged `{test}`, and `bundled_skills_direct_the_agent_to_the_authoring_harness` is tagged for other requirements. The tests are phrase-presence checks. That is a reasonable level for a static guidance document, since the behaviour of an agent following it cannot be tested deterministically. They cover each clause of the requirement.

The implementation and the tests are both complete and exact for the requirement.
